title: Wrong VLAN on an access port

scenario.title: Wrong VLAN on an access port
scenario.short: Link is up, but the server is unreachable.

network_path.source: no cable trace was collected during this investigation

initial_symptom: Application team: Server A cannot reach Server B (192.0.2.12). On-site check reports Server B's NIC link light is on.

baseline.title: Reachability srv-a → srv-b (IPv4, 56 B, ×10)
baseline.interpretation: All 10 probes from srv-a to 192.0.2.12 were answered (56-byte payload). This confirms IP reachability for packets of this size in both directions at the time of the test. It does not prove that larger packets, sustained throughput, or other flows work.

baseline.title: Reachability srv-b → srv-a (IPv4, 56 B, ×10)
baseline.interpretation: All 10 probes from srv-b to 192.0.2.11 were answered (56-byte payload). This confirms IP reachability for packets of this size in both directions at the time of the test. It does not prove that larger packets, sustained throughput, or other flows work.

baseline.title: Throughput srv-a → srv-b (10s, P1)
baseline.interpretation: Average 23.28 Gbit/s over 10 s with 0 retransmissions on a 25 Gbit/s path (MSS 8960).

baseline.title: VLAN membership — asw-2
baseline.interpretation: All data ports on asw-2 match the documented VLAN intent.
baseline.command: show vlan brief; show interface switchport

baseline.title: Interface state — asw-2:Ethernet1/1
baseline.interpretation: asw-2:Ethernet1/1 is administratively UP and operationally UP — the physical link is established at this port. A link that is up does not prove Layer 2/3 forwarding is correct.

diagnostic_actions.title: Reachability srv-a → srv-b (IPv4, 56 B, ×10)
diagnostic_actions.interpretation: No replies. The kernel reported 'Destination Host Unreachable', meaning srv-a could not resolve the link-layer address of 192.0.2.12 (ARP/ND failed). 192.0.2.12 is on-link, so this points at Layer 1/Layer 2 between the hosts — but it does not identify which element. A server that does not respond is a symptom, not proof of a broken cable.

diagnostic_actions.title: Interface state — asw-2:Ethernet1/1
diagnostic_actions.interpretation: asw-2:Ethernet1/1 is administratively UP and operationally UP — the physical link is established at this port. A link that is up does not prove Layer 2/3 forwarding is correct.

diagnostic_actions.title: Interface state — srv-b:eth0
diagnostic_actions.interpretation: srv-b:eth0 is administratively UP and operationally UP — the physical link is established at this port. A link that is up does not prove Layer 2/3 forwarding is correct.
diagnostic_actions.command: ip -d link show dev eth0; ethtool eth0 | grep -E 'Speed|Link detected'

diagnostic_actions.title: VLAN membership — asw-2
diagnostic_actions.interpretation: Running VLAN configuration differs from documented intent: Ethernet1/1 is running access VLAN 30 but the documented intent is VLAN 20 (cabled to srv-b:eth0). A host on the wrong access VLAN keeps a healthy physical link but is in a different broadcast domain, so ARP to peers in the intended VLAN fails.
diagnostic_actions.command: show vlan brief; show interface switchport
